subject: Dispute: Attribution for partial degradation during 2026-03-21 maintenance window (CloudSwitch)
messages:
From: CloudSwitch Ops <status@cloudswitch.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Skyline Health - SRE <ops@skyline-health.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident follow-up: scheduled maintenance 2026-03-21 / observed latency increase

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

Following up on the maintenance we performed in us-west-2 on 2026-03-21 (22:00-22:45 UTC). We saw a subset of requests to your customer Skyline Health show elevated p95 latency between 22:05 and 22:28 UTC. We believe the root cause was the rolling kernel patch on the egress proxies; the maintenance made a small number of connections stall while sockets were reset.

We’ve marked that time range on our incident page: https://status.cloudswitch.com/incidents/2026-03-21-maintenance. Let me know if you want the raw connection logs; we can provide a short extract.

Best,
Alex Park
CloudSwitch Operations

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident follow-up: scheduled maintenance 2026-03-21 / observed latency increase

Alex — thanks for the note. We appreciate the heads up. A couple of things:

- Skyline Health reports a measurable drop in successful requests (errors and timeouts) that persisted intermittently for ~23 minutes starting ~22:07 UTC; they’ve asked us to pursue SLA relief unless the event is explicitly excluded in the Redwood SLA.
- Our initial telemetry suggests the failure modes aligned with our inference runner reporting partial KV-cache invalidations and high token generation tail latencies (p99 spikes) for routed requests to the affected egress region.

Can you confirm exactly which IP ranges and hostnames were impacted and whether the maintenance included any third-party CDN or peering partner changes? We need the precise maintenance window, the list of hosts patched, and the raw connection traces for requests from Skyline Health (sampled request ids 1f3a... and 1f3b...).

We’ll run a quick apportionment spreadsheet and share it — attaching what we’ve prepared so far. If CloudSwitch’s maintenance overlaps but did not encompass the origin-of-failure (egress peer outage) we will contest attribution.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick response. Confirming: the maintenance was limited to our edge-proxy fleet in us-west-2. No CDN/peering configuration changes were made. Hosts patched: ws-edge-01 through ws-edge-06 (10.34.2.11-16). Official maintenance window: 22:00:00 - 22:45:00 UTC. The escalated latency you see aligns with our socket resets between 22:05:12 and 22:28:39 UTC on ws-edge-03 and ws-edge-04.

I’m attaching a small excerpt of the connection logs for the affected hosts (redacted) and a link to the full runbook we executed. If you need additional packet captures we can run a targeted export but that will take a day.

Subject: Re: Incident follow-up: scheduled maintenance 2026-03-21 / observed latency increase

Team —

I reviewed the redwood_uptime_calc_20260322.xlsx and compared Skyline Health’s request ids to CloudSwitch’s log excerpt. Two notes:

- Our apportionment model flags overlap: CloudSwitch maintenance window (22:00–22:45 UTC) covers the first ~23 minutes of Skyline’s observed failures, but Sky’s failures include a separate cluster starting 22:34 UTC that maps to a transient backend connectivity error (origin re-route) on our side (we show increased origin-5xx counts for the runner nodes handling Skyline traffic).
- Per the SLA, scheduled maintenance by an upstream provider is an exclusion only when the upstream event is the proximate cause. Given the later cluster at 22:34 UTC, we should request that CloudSwitch accept partial attribution for 22:05–22:28 UTC and allow Redwood to claim the remaining 22:34–22:46 UTC window for credit consideration.

Action items: Marcus, can you validate the origin 5xx spike and export the runner traces for 22:30–22:38 UTC? Hannah — please prepare a short note on the contractual language we’ll cite if CloudSwitch refuses partial attribution.

-Marissa

Folks —

I pulled the runner traces and packet-level handoffs for the Skyline route. Summary:
- 22:05:08–22:28:41 UTC: clear correlation between socket resets at CloudSwitch ws-edge-03/04 and connection-level retries on our side; this aligns with CloudSwitch’s log excerpt.
- 22:30:56–22:36:12 UTC: internal origin re-route caused elevated 5xx responses on two runner pods (r-nyc-prod-17, r-nyc-prod-18) while they drained and reconnected to origin; that cluster appears independent of CloudSwitch maintenance.

I recommend we propose a split attribution: CloudSwitch accepts responsibility for 22:05:08–22:28:41 UTC (apportioned uptime credit for that window) and Redwood accepts responsibility for 22:30:56–22:36:12 UTC. That leaves 22:28:41–22:30:56 UTC as a handoff/uncertain window — suggest mutual credit or no credit per contract.

Attaching the CSV snippet of traced request ids that show the transitions. If CloudSwitch agrees to the split, I can draft the technical addendum for the credit calculation and hand it to Hannah to formalize.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
